subject: Governing-law annex and dispute-exception proposal — MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Elena Park <epark@greenridge.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed governing law + venue edits for MSA

Camila —

Thanks for sending the draft. Our legal team flagged two items in the MSA that we cannot accept as written: the governing law clause (currently California) and the exclusive forum requirement. Greenridge prefers Washington law and a non-exclusive venue for urgent injunctive relief.

Attached is a redline (Greenridge_MSA_redline_v1.docx). High level:
- Governing law: change to State of Washington (King County) instead of California.
- Equitable relief: allow Greenridge to seek emergency injunctive relief in WA courts (non-waiver of arbitration).
- Arbitration: greenridge requests a mandatory arbitration only for disputes over fees and non-injunctive breaches; injunctive relief carved out.

We recognize Redwood’s desire for consistent jurisdiction language across customers. Can you confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with a narrow, time-limited injunctive exception to permit court access in WA while preserving arbitration for other claims? If not, please indicate your preferred compromise (e.g., split governing law vs. venue) and we’ll try to accommodate.

We’d like to get this wrapped before the Order Form execution next week.

Thanks —
Elena Park
Senior Counsel, Greenridge Health
Elena.Park@greenridge.com
greenridge.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Elena Park <epark@greenridge.com>
Date: 2028-12-02T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed governing law + venue edits for MSA

Camila / Elena —

Thanks for the redline and summary. I read Greenridge’s proposed edits and did a line-by-line comparison. Summary of recommended Redwood position and specific compromise language below. Please note I quote the key lines from Greenridge and follow with Redwood’s counter.

1) Governing law (Greenridge asks: Washington law)
- Redwood concern: We use California law for most enterprise contracts due to precedent and case law stability; a full swap may create cross-customer inconsistencies and precedent risks.
- Suggested compromise: Keep governing law as California, but add a narrow venue exception: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek emergency injunctive or other provisional relief in the courts of King County, Washington, without waiving any right to arbitration or other dispute resolution under this Agreement."

2) Forum & Injunctive relief (Greenridge wants non-exclusive venue for injunctive relief)
- Redwood accepts a carve for emergency injunctive relief limited to preservation of rights and temporary relief (short-duration TROs/preliminary injunction), subject to: 1) Redwood may promptly move to transfer or compel arbitration with a stay on merits claims; 2) the carve expressly excludes monetary relief claims.
- Proposed clause (redline to MSA): "For the avoidance of doubt, the arbitration provisions of this Agreement shall not preclude a party from seeking provisional remedies, including injunctive relief and orders for preservation of evidence, in a court of competent jurisdiction, provided that such remedies are limited to temporary relief and shall not determine the merits of any dispute otherwise subject to arbitration."

3) Arbitration scope (Greenridge proposes arbitration for fees only)
- Redwood prefers broad arbitration for all disputes except injunctive relief. We propose language preserving arbitration for disputes "arising out of or relating to" the Agreement, with a carve for provisional remedies as described above.

4) Practical items / Ops impact
- Mateo: If Redwood agrees to a local injunctive carve, please confirm which Redwood contacts (legal and ops) must receive notice and the expected SLA for Redwood to file a motion to stay/compel arbitration (we recommend 7 business days).

5) Next steps
- Camila: If Greenridge is willing to accept the compromise above (CA governing law + injunctive carve for WA courts), Legal can produce MSA_Greenridge_redline_v3.docx with tracked changes today.
- Recommended final: include an Order Form exhibit that states the governing law for the Order Form is the same as the MSA and references the injunctive relief carve for clarity.

I’ll attach the draft redline (MSA_Greenridge_redline_v3.docx) once finalized. Happy to jump on the call — available 11:00–11:30 PT tomorrow.

—Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0222

Camila / Laura —

Thanks for the quick read and for proposing the compromise language, Laura. Greenridge is agreeable to the California governing law with the narrow injunctive carve you proposed, with two small edits:
1) We need the clause to explicitly state injunctive relief may be sought "in the courts of King County, Washington or any federal court located in the Western District of Washington."
2) We ask that Redwood agree to a 10-business-day window to move to compel arbitration (Greenridge requests this to account for procurement counsel review).

If you can incorporate those two tweaks into your redline, we can move forward to finalize the Order Form and execute the DS for the first term. I’ll include a DocuSign link for the Order Form draft once you send the final redline.

Elena Park
Senior Counsel, Greenridge Health
